overview: Solar Generation Forecast and Dispatch addresses teams rely on lagging aggregates when forecasts or decisions depend on changing operational conditions in power and utilities operations. The first proof of value uses weather forecasts, inverter telemetry and energy schedules. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is generation forecast MAPE, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: weather forecasts, inverter telemetry and energy schedules; define generation forecast MAPE and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Grid Operations Director / Chief Asset Officer.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including backtest across seasonal and peak periods with a holdout cohort.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for generation forecast MAPE
